text_en: What then are we to say was gained by Abraham, our ancestor according to the flesh?
text_cn: 那么，我们对于按照血统作我们祖宗的亚巴郎，可以说什么呢？

text_en: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not before God.
text_cn: 如果亚巴郎是由于行为，成为义人，他就可以自夸了；但不是在天主前，

text_en: For what does the scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness. ”
text_cn: 因为经上说：“亚巴郎信了天主，天主就以此算为他的正义。”

text_en: Now to one who works, wages are not reckoned as a gift but as something due.
text_cn: 给工作的人工资，不算是恩惠，而是还债；

text_en: But to one who without works trusts him who justifies the ungodly, such faith is reckoned as righteousness.
text_cn: 但为那没有工作，而信仰那使不虔敬的人复义之主的，这人的信德为他便算是正义，这才是恩惠。

text_en: So also David speaks of the blessedness of those to whom God reckons righteousness apart from works:
text_cn: 正如达味也称那没有功行，而蒙天主恩赐算为正义的人，是有福的一样：

text_en: “Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered;
text_cn: “罪恶蒙赦免，过犯得遮掩的人，是有福的；

text_en: blessed is the one against whom the Lord will not reckon sin. ”
text_cn: 上主不归咎于他的人，是有福的。”

text_en: Is this blessedness, then, pronounced only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We say, “Faith was reckoned to Abraham as righteousness. ”
text_cn: 那么，这种福分是仅加于受割损的人呢？还是也加于未受割损的人呢？我们说过：“亚巴郎的信德为他算为正义。”

text_en: How then was it reckoned to him? Was it before or after he had been circumcised? It was not after, but before he was circumcised.
text_cn: 那么，由什么时候算起呢？是在他受割损以后呢？还是在他未受割损的时候呢？不是在他受割损以后，而是在他未受割损的时候。

text_en: He received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. The purpose was to make him the ancestor of all who believe without being circumcised and who thus have righteousness reckoned to them,
text_cn: 他后来领受了割损的标记，只是作为他未受割损时，因信德获得正义的印证。如此，亚巴郎作了一切未受割损而相信的人的父亲，使他们也同样因信德而算为正义；

text_en: and likewise the ancestor of the circumcised who are not only circumcised but who also follow the example of the faith that our ancestor Abraham had before he was circumcised.
text_cn: 同时也作受割损者的父亲，就是那些不仅受割损，而且也追随我们的祖宗亚巴郎，在未受割损时所走的信德之路的人。

text_en: For the promise that he would inherit the world did not come to Abraham or to his descendants through the law but through the righteousness of faith.
text_cn: 因为许给亚巴郎和他的后裔的恩许，使他作世界的承继者，并不是藉着法律，而是藉着因信德而获得的正义，

text_en: If it is the adherents of the law who are to be the heirs, faith is null and the promise is void.
text_cn: 因为假使属于法律的人才是承继者，那么信德便是空虚的，恩许就失了效力，

text_en: For the law brings wrath; but where there is no law, neither is there violation.
text_cn: 因为法律只能激起天主的义怒：哪里没有法律，那里就没有违犯。

text_en: For this reason it depends on faith, in order that the promise may rest on grace and be guaranteed to all his descendants, not only to the adherents of the law but also to those who share the faith of Abraham (for he is the father of all of us,
text_cn: 为此，一切都是由于信德，为的是一切都本着恩宠，使恩许为亚巴郎所有的一切后裔坚定不移，不仅为那属于法律的后裔，而且也为那有亚巴郎信德的后裔，因为他是我们众人的父亲，

text_en: as it is written, “I have made you the father of many nations”)—in the presence of the God in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls into existence the things that do not exist.
text_cn: 正如经上所载：“我已立你为万民之父；”亚巴郎是在他所信的天主面前，就是在叫死者复活，叫那不存在的成为存在的那位面前，作我们众人的父亲。

text_en: Hoping against hope, he believed that he would become “the father of many nations, ” according to what was said, “So numerous shall your descendants be. ”
text_cn: 他在绝望中仍怀着希望而相信了，因此便成了万民之父，正如向他所预许的：“你的后裔也要这样多。”

text_en: He did not weaken in faith when he considered his own body, which was already as good as dead (for he was about a hundred years old), or when he considered the barrenness of Sarah’s womb.
text_cn: 他虽然快一百岁，明知自己的身体已经衰老，撒辣的胎也已绝孕；但他的信心却没有衰弱，

text_en: No distrust made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God,
text_cn: 对于天主的恩许总没有因不信而犹疑，反而信心坚固，归光荣于天主，

text_en: being fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised.
text_cn: 且满心相信天主所应许的，必予完成。

text_en: Therefore his faith “was reckoned to him as righteousness. ”
text_cn: 天主就以此算为他的正义。

text_en: Now the words, “it was reckoned to him, ” were written not for his sake alone,
text_cn: “算为他的正义”这句话，不是单为他个人写的，

text_en: but for ours also. It will be reckoned to us who believe in him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
text_cn: 而且也是为了我们这些将来得算为正义的人，即我们这些相信天主使我们的主耶稣，由死者中复活的人写的；

text_en: who was handed over to death for our trespasses and was raised for our justification.
text_cn: 这耶稣曾为了我们的过犯被交付，又为了使我们成义而复活。
